gap: No result ChatGPT got states that once a LiFePO4 battery's BMS cuts off for over-discharge the terminals show no output, and only a charger with an activation ('wake-up', 'boost' or '0V') function can push the small current that brings it back; a plain charger that is merely LiFePO4-rated may not start.
standout_why: I opened the Bixpower LF1220 kit page (result 5), which is the only rival kit page I could read. It gives the roughly 10 V cutoff and the 0–45 °C charge window but nothing on recovering after a cutoff. ChatGPT's own answer only says to use a 14.6 V LiFePO4-specific charger. The Chameleon kit page (429), the epowerguys Dakota pages (429) and the Dakota Powerbox PDF on nationwide-battery.com (binary text that could not be read) were not checked, so I can't rule out that one of them mentions it.
decides: This fact doesn't change the pick yet. It adds a filter: a 12 V kit is only safe for a battery that may be run flat (trolling motor, Power Wheels, a camper left in storage) if its charger has a 0V/activation mode. Search snippets say the Redodo 20A, Power Queen 20A and ECO-WORTHY 20A chargers all have one, but I couldn't open any of those maker pages, so none of them can be confirmed or ruled out on this point.

findings.label: What happens after a BMS over-discharge cutoff
findings.value: Below the BMS over-discharge threshold 'the protection lockout may be triggered, causing the battery to have no output'
findings.source_title: How to Jumpstart a Dead Lithium LiFePO4 Battery? (LiTime)
findings.note: A battery maker's (LiTime's) support blog, dated Aug 17, 2026. The byline says John Marius but the author bio names John Thompson. It gives no numeric threshold.

findings.label: How a cut-off battery is brought back
findings.value: A charger with a 'wake-up', 'boost' or '0V' function 'delivers a low, controlled current to safely reactivate a battery with BMS protection'; an over-discharged battery 'can usually be restored by using a charger with an activation function'
findings.source_title: How to Jumpstart a Dead Lithium LiFePO4 Battery? (LiTime)
findings.note: Same page. It also warns that a regular jump starter 'can send too much current to the battery', and says that if the voltage doesn't rise after several tries the battery may be permanently damaged.
